bullets: Nasdaq/S&P had their worst day since 2020 Thu as a Democratic midterm sweep stoked AI-regulation and data-center-moratorium fears; Mag7 lost ~$1T.
VIX spiked ~70% to 28.2; Fri futures mixed, Nasdaq fut recovering slightly (+0.4%) while S&P/Dow futures stay soft.
Oil rebounding (Brent +~4%) on renewed US-Iran conflict risk after an 8% Wednesday drop; 10Y yield eased near 4.84% on safe-haven buying.
October jobs report due 8:30am ET (payrolls 65K est, unemployment 4.2%) is today's key swing factor for the risk-off mood.

AVTR.why: Q3 beat (EPS/revenue above estimates, organic-growth guidance raised) but FY adjusted EPS guidance merely matched consensus; investors read it as uninspiring, triggering a sell-the-news drop. No downgrade, no miss.
AVTR.bull: Core Q3 beat with raised organic-growth guidance shows underlying demand improving, setting up a bounce from oversold levels.
AVTR.bear: Guidance merely matched consensus with flat margins, so the post-earnings de-rating could persist without a fresh catalyst.

GKOS.why: Four firms raised price targets to Buy/Overweight on 2026-10-29 after a strong quarter; drop looks like profit-taking plus notable insider selling ($16.5M/90 days) rather than company damage. No downgrade or bad news found.
GKOS.bull: All four analysts raised price targets after a record quarter, implying Wall Street sees the pullback as pure profit-taking.
GKOS.bear: Heavy insider selling and reportedly bearish options flow suggest some holders expect pressure to persist near-term.

PBF.why: Energy sector fell ~10% broadly (oil volatility from US-Iran tension) matching PBF's drop. Only one Hold-level upgrade and one maintained Neutral found, both with raised price targets; no PBF-specific bad news.
PBF.bull: Energy sector-wide selloff, not PBF-specific news, drove the drop; refining cash-flow and growth narrative remain intact.
PBF.bear: Refining margins are cyclical and oil-price swings from Iran tensions could keep pressuring crack spreads and the stock.

PSX.why: Drop tracks a broad energy-sector slide (~10% sector move) tied to oil volatility, not company news. Analysts (Citi, Morgan Stanley, Wells Fargo, Freedom Broker) all maintained/raised ratings and targets through early November.
PSX.bull: Drop tracks a broad energy-sector slide; analysts kept raising price targets (Citi, Morgan Stanley, Wells Fargo) through early November.
PSX.bear: A renewed Iran conflict could whipsaw oil and refining margins, adding volatility before the position can play out.

RVTY.why: Q3 beat with raised 2026 guidance, yet shares round-tripped (fell then rallied ~11%) on valuation concerns (GF Value implies ~35% overvalued, P/E 74x vs 5yr median 36x). No miss, no downgrade, just a company-specific valuation debate.
RVTY.bull: Q3 beat with raised 2026 guidance and multiple analyst PT hikes point to improving fundamentals beneath the valuation debate.
RVTY.bear: Stock is viewed as richly valued (GF Value implies ~35% downside), so good news may keep getting sold.

CVLT.why: Drop mirrors the broad software-sector rout (-8% to -10% sector-wide) tied to AI-regulation fears after the midterms, not Commvault news. Four firms maintained/upgraded with raised price targets on 2026-10-28; SaaS growth story intact.
CVLT.bull: Drop mirrors a broad software-sector rout tied to AI-regulation fears, not any Commvault-specific news; SaaS growth story intact.
CVLT.bear: If AI-driven software de-rating continues market-wide, CVLT could keep falling with peers regardless of its own fundamentals.

HPQ.why: Intel warned PC shipments will fall 12% in 2026/10% in 2027, hitting Dell (-11%), HPE, Supermicro and HP (-7-9%) together - sector-wide, not HP-specific. Adds uncertainty: new, untested CEO Emma Walmsley named 2026-11-04; no dd.moves found.
HPQ.bull: HP's slide mostly reflects Intel's industry-wide PC-demand warning that hit Dell and HPE too, not an HP-only problem.
HPQ.bear: A new, untested CEO plus a structurally weakening PC market make the fundamental setup for a bounce weaker.

BRKR.why: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS beat ($0.56 vs $0.42 est), guidance maintained; GAAP headline loss was due to a one-time non-cash $175M goodwill impairment. Two firms (Citi, Leerink) raised price targets 2026-11-05; broader medical-device-sector selloff also hit peers.
BRKR.bull: Adjusted EPS beat, maintained full-year guidance, and two analyst price-target hikes show the core business is healthy.
BRKR.bear: A $175M non-cash goodwill impairment and a broad medical-device-sector selloff add noise that could delay the bounce.

IEX.bear: Drop tracks a broader industrials pullback; continued macro risk-off into the weekend's jobs report could extend the slide.
